transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Well, I came in because... ever since my wife’s fall, things have just fallen apart. I've always been the man with the lists and the plan, you know? But lately, I just end up sitting at the kitchen table, staring at her medication chart. I'll start crying, or I'm snapping over absolutely nothing. And I'm just letting everything go. The bills, my mentoring calls, even basic housework... it's all just piling up. I just can’t seem to make myself function right now.
How long has it been since your wife's fall?

It was only about two months ago. And... well, I was doing fine before that. I really only started falling apart after she got hurt and the whole daily caregiving routine took over. That's when all this started, not before.
In addition to the sadness and crying spells you mentioned, have you been feeling unusually nervous, restless, or unable to relax?

No, I wouldn't say I feel nervous or restless. It's not really like that. I'm not pacing the floors or feeling jittery or anything. I guess I'm not exactly relaxed either, but it's more because I just feel so... heavy, you know? Like I mentioned, I just sit there. But no, I haven't noticed feeling unusually anxious or nervous.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your sleep patterns or your appetite since your wife's accident?
No, my sleep and appetite have been pretty much the same. I still eat my regular meals, and I'm sleeping through the night like I usually do. I haven't noticed any real changes there.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in the activities that you used to enjoy?

No, not really. I mean, I haven't really had the time to do much of anything I used to enjoy anyway, with taking care of my wife and all. But I don't think I've lost interest in those things. I just... I don't have the energy or the time right now. If I had a free afternoon, I'd still want to read or work in the garden, I just can't seem to get to it.
Do you feel that the distress you are experiencing is significantly out of proportion to the severity of your wife's situation?

No, I wouldn't say that. I mean... her situation is pretty severe. She needs a lot of care, and our whole life has been turned upside down. I think feeling this overwhelmed makes sense given what we're actually going through. It doesn't feel out of proportion to me, no.
